

PREFACE
The Member airlines of the International Air Transport Association (IATA) and the
Airlines for America (A4A) have developed the Standard IATA/A4A Cargo
Interchange Message Procedures (Cargo-IMP).
The purpose of this Manual is to enable communication which will ensure
uniformity, understanding, accuracy and economy. The Manual is published as
Attachment ‘A’ to IATA Resolution 670.



The 34th Edition of the IATA Cargo Interchange Message Procedures Manual
becomes effective on 1 January 2014 and replaces the previous 33rd Edition.



As per the IATA Cargo Services Conference (CSC), there will be no further
changes to Cargo-IMP Messages and the Cargo-IMP 34th edition is the last and
final edition. From now on, any future changes in the messages will only be
conducted in the Cargo-XML standards that are available in the IATA Cargo-XML
Manual and Toolkit.



Users are advised that the Cargo-IMP functionality is improved by allowing
exchange of ASCII 7 bit characters.



Users are further advised that additional editorial corrections have been made to
the Status Answer (FSA) and the Status Update (FSU) messages.
These procedures are consistent with the requirements of the IATA Systems and
Communications Reference Manuals as they relate to technical communications
procedures, and with IATA and A4A Cargo Resolutions, as they relate to cargo
processes.
Source Documents take precedence over codes published in this Manual.
Messages in the Cargo-IMP format will be accepted by both IATA Members and
A4A Members.
Proposals for new messages or amendments to existing messages published in the
Cargo-IMP Manual shall be submitted to the Cargo Business Processes Panel
(CBPP), on the standard form which is Attachment ‘A’ of Resolution 671 and is
included with this Preface.
The grey shaded background indicates amendments that have not yet been
declared effective at time of production. They are awaiting the necessary
government approvals.
Any comments concerning the content of the Manual would be appreciated. Users
of the Manual are invited to contact (YMQFPXB or cargoedi@iata.org) for any
technical assistance required in the implementation and use of these messages.

INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETION
Data ID — organise data by logical, related groups and enter either:
an upper case letter to identify the data group; or
a sequential number for each data element.
Data Description — enter a concise, meaningful description of the data group or
the data element.
Form — enter the character type (a – alpha, n – numeric, an – alphanumeric, d –
decimal, t – text) for the data element and the number, or minimum/maximum
range, e.g. 4...8, of characters.
Status — enter one of the following statuses for the data group or data element:
— mandatory (must be included);
— conditional (must be included if the indicated condition is met);
— optional (may be included).
The status of the data element is relevant to the status of the data group. For
example, within an optional data group, the condition for a conditional data element
only applies if the optional data group is included.
For EDIFACT messages, only mandatory and conditional statuses apply.
Condition — if the status of the data group or element is “C”, enter the condition
for the inclusion of the data group or data element. The condition must be related
strictly to the existence, or non-existence, of other data within the message.
Note — if further explanation for a data group or data element is required, enter a
sequential reference number and include the explanatory note on a separate sheet
of paper.
Repeat Information — if multiple occurrences of data are allowed, complete this
as follows:

Data — enter the Data ID, or range of Data IDs, of the data group(s) or data
element(s) that can be repeated;
Times — enter the number of times the data can be repeated. If unlimited
occurrences are allowed, enter “U”;
Within — for data repetition within a data group or within another data repetition
range, enter the Data ID, or range of Data IDs, of the data group(s).

GENERAL INFORMATION
1. FUNCTION OF CARGO-IMP MESSAGES
The Cargo-IMP messages have been developed by the Member Airlines of the
International Air Transport Association (IATA) and the Airlines for America (A4A) as
Standard IATA/A4A Cargo Interchange Message Procedures. The purpose of
these messages is to ensure uniformity, mutual understanding, accuracy and
economy in inter-airline data exchange and in data exchange between airlines and
other air cargo industry participants including agents, brokers and Customs. The
messages are used in both manual and computerized environments.
The messages are consistent with the A4A/IATA Cargo Resolutions as they relate
to Cargo Procedures.



Note: IATA has now developed and published the Cargo-XML Messages. For
further details visit IATA Cargo-XML webpage at www.iata.org/Cargo-XML.

2. TERMINOLOGY
For the purposes of this Manual the following terminology will be used:

2.1 Transmission
A transmission consists of the data (information) that is interchanged at one time
between parties.

2.2 Message
A message is the lowest unit of complete information that may be exchanged
between an originator and a recipient for a predefined purpose.

2.3 Standard Message Identifier (SMI)
An SMI is an approved three-letter code which is used to uniquely identify a given
type of message. It must always be shown at the beginning of a Standard Message
Text and appears separately on the first line after the address envelope.

2.4 Standard Message Text (SMT)
A Standard Message Text (SMT) contains the information required for a predefined
purpose. It is composed of a number of related text elements structured according
to agreed standards. The sequence in which elements are grouped is determined
by the logical progression required for computer processing as well as manual
reading.

2.5 Text Element
A text element is a basic unit for the transmission of data and is composed of a
group of related data elements.

2.6 Text Element Identifier (Line Identifier)
A three-letter identifier used at the beginning of a line to indicate that certain data
elements will follow.

2.7 Data Group
A data group consists of either one or several data elements with or without
separators. It shows the interdependence of data within a text element and allows
the group to be shown as optional, conditional or mandatory.

2.8 Data Element (Simple and Composite)
A data element is an item of information that has been uniquely identified for the
interchange of data. A data element may be either a Simple or a Composite Data
Element.
Simple Data Element — One unit of data, providing a single concept, e.g.
Month MAR.
Composite Data
— A combination of more than one unit of data,
Element
providing a broad concept, e.g. Full Date
DDMMMYY 12MAR85.

2.9 Data Element Identifier
A one, two, three or four-letter identifier used to identify the Data Element which
follows.

2.10 Optional
The Text Element/Data Group/Data Element may be included at the option of the
sender or by agreement between sender and recipient.

2.11 Conditional
The Text Element/Data Group/Data Element is required dependent upon a stated
condition.

2.12 Mandatory
The Text Element/Data Group/Data Element must be included.

2.13 Separator Character
A special character which serves as a separator between Data Elements/Data
Groups/Text Elements.

2.14 Syntax Rules
The agreed rules governing the structure of a transmission.

3. TRANSMISSION OF CARGO-IMP MESSAGES
3.1 Various Applications for Message Utilisation
A Cargo-IMP Message may be utilised in the following ways:
3.1.1 Computer-to-Computer
The Cargo-IMP Message is automatically constructed and generated by the
sending party and will be automatically processed by the receiving party.
3.1.2 Manual-to-Computer
The Cargo-IMP Message is manually constructed and generated by the sending
party and will be automatically processed by the receiving party.
3.1.3 Computer-to-Manual
The Cargo-IMP Message is automatically constructed and generated by the
sending party and will be manually processed by the receiving party.
3.1.4 Manual-to-Manual
The Cargo-IMP Message is manually constructed and generated by the sending
party and will be manually processed by the receiving party.

4. DESCRIPTION OF CARGO-IMP MESSAGES — SYNTAX RULES
4.1 Composition of Cargo-IMP Messages
A Cargo-IMP Message is composed of a Message Address, a Standard Message
Identifier (SMI) and a Standard Message Text (SMT). The Standard Message
Identifier is shown separately on the first line of the Cargo-IMP Message.
The structure of Cargo-IMP Messages is such that they can be easily prepared and
read in both manual and computerized environments.
Cargo-IMP Messages are constructed with due regard to transmission costs and
therefore the number of characters is kept to a minimum.

4.2 Description of Cargo-IMP Messages
The message descriptions/specifications contained in the message chapters of this
manual detail the SMI and the sequential order of data elements that form a
Standard Message Text (SMT). The sequential order is determined by the logical
progression of elements required for computer processing and also the
requirements of manual reading.



(including FWB version 16) can use ASCII 7 bit (Table 4.3.1) characters while

messages published in lower editions of the Cargo-IMP Manual can continue using
the limited characters.
Cargo-IMP Messages published in Cargo-IMP Manual 31st edtion and lower
(except FWB version 16) can only contain the following approved characters:
the letters A to Z (upper case only)
the numerals 0 to 9
the special characters / -. Space < =

4.4 Separator Characters
Some of the approved characters are used for specific functions within the
message.
The slant (/) is used as an element separator. The slant is also used as the first
character position on a line to indicate that the data which follows is a continuation
of related data in the preceding line, i.e. the data has only been entered on a
separate line because of the line length constraints.
The hyphen (-) is used as a sub-element separator.
The full stop (.) is used as a decimal point within data elements.
The carriage return line feed (< =) is used to separate lines of information. Where
possible, a “line” contains a complete logical group of information.



4.6 Identification within a Cargo-IMP Message
Data within a Cargo-IMP message is identified in one of two ways:
(a) Implicitly — by position in a fixed sequence;
(b) Explicitly — by use of a Data Element or Text Element Identifier (Line
Identifier).
Data Element Identifiers consist of one or more characters.
Text Element Identifiers (Line Identifiers) consist of three characters and identify a
single line or the first line in a sequence of lines. These identifiers are always
followed by a separator (/).

4.7 Specification of Content of a Cargo-IMP Message
For the purpose of this manual the following symbols are used to define the status
of the Element:
O — Optional (see 2.10)
C — Conditional (see 2.11)
M — Mandatory (see 2.12).
The elements in the message are grouped by levels where:
Level 1 is the Text Element Level
Level 2 is the Data Group Level
Level 3 is the Data Element Level.
Each element is allocated a numeric reference within the Cargo-IMP Message. For
example, a ULD Description might be:

4.8 Length of a Cargo-IMP Message
A Cargo-IMP Message is restricted to a maximum of 3500 characters.
Each line within a Cargo-IMP Message is restricted to a maximum of 69 characters.

4.9 Split of a Cargo-IMP Message
If a message is longer than 3500 characters, the method used to split the message
text is dependent on the Message Identifier.
4.9.1 Method 1
For Airline Flight Manifest (FFM), Booking List (FBL) and Declaration for Dangerous
Goods Data (FDD) Messages the following method is used:
First Part:
(a) the first line of the Standard Message Text (SMT) must contain sequence
number: 1
(b) the Standard Message Text (SMT) must terminate with the line: CONT < =
Following Parts:
(a) the first line of the Standard Message Text (SMT) must contain the next
sequential number: N
(b) the Standard Message Text (SMT) must terminate with the line:
either CONT < = if other part to follow
or LAST < = if the last part
Note:
If the message has only 1 part, the SMT terminates with the line: LAST < =
4.9.2 Method 2
For all other messages, the following method is used:

First Part:
must terminate with the extra line:
PART/1/CONT < =
Following Parts:
(a) must commence with the SMI plus the first line of the Standard Message Text
(SMT)
(b) must terminate with the extra line:
• either PART/N/CONT < =
• if other part to follow
• or PART/N/LAST < =
• if the last part

4.10 Illustration of Standard Form Structure

5. TEXT ELEMENTS FOR FREE TEXT DATA
There are two special text elements which occur in several Cargo-IMP Messages.
These text elements commence with a text element identifier (SSR or OSI) followed
by a separator (/) and terminate with a CRLF (< =). These text elements are:
(a) SSR — Special Service Request (special manual action required message will
have to be routed for manual processing);

(b) OSI — Other Service Information (can simply be stored as remarks —
message does not have to be routed for any special action).

6. VALIDATION OF A CARGO-IMP MESSAGE
6.1 Validation of Data to be Built into a Cargo-IMP Message
In a computer environment validation checks according to the Resolutions and/or
Recommended Practices published in the IATA Cargo Services Conference
Resolutions Manual should be applied prior to building data into a Cargo-IMP
message.

6.2 Validation of the Structure of a Cargo-IMP Message
Before a message is transmitted, certain validation routines are performed on the
message in order to minimize the possible errors in message composition. The
validation routines include:
(a) verification of the length of the message;
(b) verification of the length of each line in the message;
(c) verification of the characters used in the message.
6.2.1 Validation of Repeated Data
Within the message specifications there is sometimes an allowance for data to be
repeated. Unless the number of occurrences is specified, e.g. Can occur a
maximum of three times, the number of repeats is unlimited but must adhere to the
following:



(a) the maximum 69 characters per line and 3500 characters per message as
specified in 4.8;
(b) a specific note limiting the total number of characters within the data group or
reference line.

7. RETRANSMITTAL OF A MESSAGE
When a receiving station requests that a message be retransmitted, the
retransmitted message text may start with the code “PDM” followed by a Carriage
Return Line Feed.
When a sender or sending system retransmits a message because of a lack of
confirmation of receipt, the retransmitted message text must start with the code
“PDM” followed by a Carriage Return Line Feed.

8. CORRECTION OF INVALID/INCORRECT REFERENCE NUMBER
When the receiving system cannot action the incoming message due to an invalid
or incorrect prime reference number, i.e. AWB Identification, Embargo Number or
ULD Reference Number, it is recommended that the standard Cargo-IMP Error
(FNA) Message is transmitted to the sender of the message.

10. TRANSMISSION OF CARGO-IMP MESSAGES THROUGH AIRLINE
DATA EXCHANGE NETWORKS

When a Cargo-IMP Message is transmitted through the airline data exchange
networks it is “enveloped” between a “Message Address” header (comprising a
message priority indicator, one or more address groups, an origin group and a
date/time group) and an “End of Message” trailer.
The definition of the airline data exchange networks envelope is contained in the
IATA Systems and Communications Reference Manual. The following descriptions
are extracted from, or are in line with, the information contained in that Manual.

10.1 Message Address (Header) Format

10.2 Message Priority Indicator
The following “Priority Indicators” may be included in a position prior to the first
address in the address section:
Indicator
QU
QP

Precedence
URGENT
NORMAL

Note:
The nature of the traffic bearing this priority indicator is such that the originator deems
that it should be given special attention in local delivery, and that this delivery should
not be delayed.
QK

NORMAL

Note:
Default for ‘normal’ message traffic. QK has same precedence as messages bearing
no priority indicator.
QD

DEFERRED

The Priority Indicators QX and QS have distinct meanings in some systems; QX is
used for urgent operational traffic and QS for top precedence messages pertaining
to the safety of human life.

10.3 Address and Origin Groups
The Address and Origin Groups consist of seven-character groups (these may be
extended to eight-letter groups in the future) of which:
(a) the first three letters shall be a Location Identifier;
(b) the fourth and fifth characters denote the Office Function Designator
(department) within the airline;
(c) the sixth and seventh characters (or sixth, seventh and eighth letters when
used) denote the airline, or appropriate organization.
Note:
Where automated carriers require particular Cargo-IMP Messages to be sent to a
specific SITA/ARINC address, address details are included in the appropriate message
description contained in the individual message chapter.

10.4 Message Identity
The message identity is used by the originator to identify the message. There is no
standard format although the date/time is often used. The message identity can
include any alphanumeric characters plus the full stop (with the exception of upper
case H and upper case D).
The use of the oblique (/) character in the message identity is not recommended. If
there is no double signature, the message identity must not include an oblique (/)
character as the third character following 2 letters as this is read as a double
signature.
If the date/time group is used in the message identity, the time must be expressed
in UTC.

i.e. Cargo-IMP and EDIFACT, all messages routed through CCSs are “wrapped” in
a standardized EDIFACT envelope as shown below.

11.7 Cargo-IMP Messages Transmitted Under EDIFACT Envelope
Cargo-IMP messages routed through CCSs are wrapped within the EDIFACT
envelope as explained below.

11.8 Wrapping of Cargo-IMP Messages
Each fraction of 5 lines of a Cargo-IMP Message will be included in a FTX segment
with the resulting FTX segment(s) preceded by a UNH segment and terminated by
a UNT segment.
When packing these fractions of 5 Cargo-IMP lines into one FTX segment the
various CRLFs shall be replaced by “ : ” except the last one which will be replaced
by “ ’ ”.

11.9 Example of Wrapping of Cargo-IMP Message
(a) Cargo-IMP message before wrapping:

12. RETURN INFORMATION FIELD (‘RIF’) ADDRESSING STANDARD
FOR CCS/PARTICIPANT COMMUNICATION
For messages which are converted between EDIFACT and Cargo-IMP standards,
and then routed to/ from CCS ‘participant’ systems, the ‘RIF’ Standard is applied in
order to retain ‘PIMA’ address information within the message envelopes. CCS
‘participant’ is defined within this context as an airline or user of a SITA/ARINC
Type ‘B’ connection.
The ‘RIF’ Standard provides the transfer, upon message conversion, of ‘PIMA’ data
between the EDIFACT envelope and the Type ‘B’ IATA envelope. This transfer is
necessary in order to retain sender and addressee address information throughout
the message transmission cycle, from sender to destination and back via the
response message, and several CCSs as necessary.
The following benefits accrue to airline CCS users, through the use of the ‘RIF’
Standard:

— provides onward routing of messages to parties who do not have their own
SITA/ARINC address, but who support EDIFACT envelopes; and
— allows unique identification of EDIFACT end-users for purposes of security
checking (ex. to check if a party requesting a booking is authorized to do so);
Similarly the following benefits accrue to agents:
— enables a requesting agent to forward the message response to the originating
customers’ terminal/file/representative.

12.1 Description of the ‘RIF’ Standard — EDIFACT Envelope
The following is return address information which is structured within the EDIFACT
UNB Segment:

the end of the Double Signature Group.

13. PRESENTATION OF DIRECTORY
13.1 Presentation of Data Elements in the Directory
Each identified data element has been given:
(a) a data element name;
(b) a description of the concept to explain the agreed meaning and to aid in
determining the content of the information (data item) to be provided with the
data element;

(c) a specification of the character representation of the data item, with indication
of space (in number of characters) available and, when applicable or required:
(d) references which refer users to other parts of the Directory, or to other sources,
as appropriate;
(e) synonyms of data element names where such are widely used.
It is assumed that most data elements can be expressed either in plain language or
in code, and it is recognized that there will be a need to refer to either of these
versions, and sometimes to both.
Mainly for identification and management purposes, each data element is provided
with a numeric identifier (tag).

13.2 Layout of Data Element Entries
The first line of each data element entry contains the numeric tag and the second
line contains the name of the data element.
In addition, each data element entry contains a number of parts, identified by a
header. The following headers are used to designate the different parts of the
entries:
“Alt. Name”
“Description”
“Format”
“Cargo-IMP Ref.”
“Note”

= synonymous names of the data element;
= description of the data element;
= character representation, space available;
= reference to an indicated source of information
— usually the Coding section;
= additional information, when appropriate.

Data element entries are separated from each other by a line.

13.3 Abbreviations of Character Representations
See Element Character Format of General Information for more details concerning
the abbreviations used to explain character representation.

14. CATEGORIES OF DATA ELEMENTS
14.1 Categories of Data Elements, Allocation of Identifiers (Tags)
Three-digit numbers are used as data element identifiers (tags) in the Directory.
Taking into account the desirability of grouping the data elements into broad
categories in a way that will assist users of the Directory, the numbers have been
assigned as follows:
(a) 000 to 099 are not used;
(b) 100 to 999 are used for random allocation of tags to the data elements, within
the framework of a sub-division into 9 general categories, as specified in 14.3.
The purpose of the tags is to provide language independent identifiers for the data

elements; the only significance attributed to the numbers is their designation of
broad categories.

14.2 Grouping of Data Elements into Broad Categories
The system selected for the Directory for grouping data elements into broad
categories is based on the characteristics of the data item, taking into account its
nature rather than its application area. This means that all dates are placed in one
group, all names in another, and all amounts in a third, without any consideration of
the kind of date, name and amount.
Users, even if they do not know the exact name of a data element, or in which
application area a particular data element might have been placed, are likely to
know the expected contents of the data item with sufficient accuracy to be able to
find it within a limited range of not more than one hundred data elements placed
together according to this principle.

14.3 Category Description
As set out in 14.2 the data elements have been grouped into broad categories in a
way that will assist users of the Directory, at the same time taking into account the
need to reserve substantial capacity for future newly defined data elements.
The following grouping is used in the Directory:
Group 1: (100–149) Documentation, references
Data elements intended for data handling or documentation
purposes, such as document and message names,
references and reference numbers, ordinal numbers such
as item and page numbers, number of copies of documents.
Group 2: (200–249) Dates, times, periods of time
All expressions of time, such as calendar dates, periods of
time (month, week, day), time limits, commencement and
expiry dates.
Group 3: (300–349) Parties, addresses, places, countries
Names and addresses of legal and physical persons,
designations of officials, organizational units, places,
countries, routes.
Group 4: (400–449) Clauses, conditions, terms, instructions
Authentications, authorizations, endorsements,
certifications, clauses, conditions, terms, reference clauses,
stamps, labels, requests, instructions, receipts, statements,
information texts.
Group 5: (500–549) Amounts, charges, percentages
Financial values, amounts, charges; other quantities and
values for commercial, transport, customs, statistical and

any other purposes; other details such as prices, rates,
percentages and discounts, used as a basis for invoice
calculations, etc.
Group 6: (600–649) Measure identifiers, quantities (other than
monetary)
Dimensions, weights, volumes, distances, temperature,
currency, other quantities, with the exception of monetary
quantities in Group 5, measure unit specifiers.
Group 7: (700–749) Goods and articles: descriptions and identifiers
Descriptions, classifications and identification of goods and
articles, consignment identifiers, number and kind of
packages, dangerous goods details.
Group 8: (800–849) Transport modes and means, ULDs (aircraft
containers and pallets)
Identification and description of means of transport and
ULDs, transport equipment details, transport modes and
movements, voyage and flight numbers.
Group 9: (900–949) External Requirements (Customs, etc.)
Data elements used for the interchange of information with
external parties such as Customs Authorities, Agents, etc.

14.4 Sub-Data Elements
The Sub-Data Elements represent the description used to identify the variations of
the Data Elements used in the “Element” column of the Message Specifications.

15. MESSAGE TYPE VERSION NUMBERS
The Message Type Version Number was first introduced in the 9th Edition of the
Cargo-IMP Manual. All new Message Specifications in that Edition, and those that
had been amended from the 8th Edition, included a Message Type Version
Number.
All other messages do not include the version number .

Message Exchange Parties can be airlines or third parties (such as handling
agents) with computer systems that are capable of interchanging Cargo-IMP
Messages.
The individual user tables indicate the information available at the time of
publication of this Edition of the CIMP. Any additional information may be obtained
from the author, whose address is included in the Preface of this product.
As the Cargo-IMP users included may not be exhaustive, parties are asked to send
identification of further Cargo-IMP users to the author as well.

The user tables contain the message version numbers for Cargo-IMP messages
supported by users of the Cargo-IMP standard.
Cargo-IMP users are presented as two separate groups:
• Airlines
• Forwarders, Handling Agents and Third Parties
Two addresses are indicated:
• the address for the Cargo Control Computer
• the address for the Cargo Data Interchange Coordinator for each system
For parties wishing to exchange messages with airlines, it is recommended that
communication first be made with the Airline Respondant/Coordinator indicated.

17. “GENERAL” NOTES
Introduction to “General” Notes
The specification for each Cargo-IMP message includes a “Note” column. Most
notes referenced in the column are specific to one message, e.g. FWB1 or FFM1.
“Message Specific” notes and “Conditional and Qualification” notes are found at the
end of each message specification.
Some notes apply to several messages. These notes are referred to a “General”
notes. They are referenced in the message specification “Note” column as “GEN1”,
“GEN2” etc. The “General” notes are listed below.

GEN1 — Split of Cargo-IMP Messages
Cargo-IMP Messages are limited to a maximum length of 3500 characters.
A general message split procedure is used for messages which may exceed 3500
characters (except for FFM and FBL messages which have been designed with a
multi-part format).
The general message split procedure is described in 4.9.2 of Chapter 1 of the

Manual.

GEN2 — Dates and Times in Cargo-IMP Messages
Dates and times in Cargo-IMP messages are given in the “local time” at the place
at which the associated action occurs.
UTC (Universal Coordinated Time) is only used in the messages relating to
Embargos (FMB, FMC, FMX) where the Start of Embargo and End of Embargo are
specified as Date (in UTC) and Time (in UTC).

GEN3 — Length of Consignment Detail Line
In order to achieve a logical grouping of consignment data the “Consignment
Detail” line has been defined with a theoretical maximum line length of 71
characters, i.e. the Cargo-IMP maximum line length of 69 characters has been
exceeded.
It is considered extremely unlikely that all the data elements in the Consignment
Detail line will be included at their maximum length. However, should this
circumstance arise the one (or two) least significant characters will be “dropped”
from the Nature of Goods data element to reduce the line length back to 69
characters.

GEN4 — Airline and Company Designators
The actual format is either aa, na or an. For future planning purposes, it should be
noted that the format may become “aaa”.

GEN5 — Airline and Company Designators
The two-character format (aa, na or an) may be used instead of the three-character
format (aaa).

GEN6 — Credit Card Masking
As per "Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards(PCI DSS)", masking shall
be applicable to the credit card number display, a maximum of the first six and last
four digits (1234 56XX XXXX 7890) can be displayed.

18. CCC/IATA CUSTOMS-AIRLINES MESSAGES
This Manual contains the Customs-Airlines Messages that were developed and
agreed by the Joint Project undertaken by the Customs Cooperation Council (CCC)
and IATA.
The interchange of data between Customs and Airlines is governed by a
Memorandum of Understanding between the CCC and IATA, a CCC
Recommendation and by IATA CSC Resolution 656.
The CCC/IATA Message Specifications contained in this Manual are amended
versions to the message specifications published in Appendix ‘A’ of the CCC/IATA

Joint Customs/Airlines Electronic Data Interchange Manual.
These CCC/IATA Message Specifications replace the Development Proposals for
Airline Customs Messages that have been published in previous Editions of the
Cargo-IMP Manual.
Users planning to develop or implement these Messages are requested to contact
the Secretariat.

9. CUSTOMS INVENTORY REPORT MESSAGE LAYOUT

CUSTOMS SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (CSI) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = CSI
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To update or amend consignment information for:
• a simple air waybill (covering a single shipment);
• a master air waybill (covering a group of consolidated “house” shipments);
• an individual “house” waybill (where the airline is breaking down a consolidation and
will control and deliver at the house waybill level);
supplied to Customs in a CIR and/or previous CSI messages.
2.2 To cancel a Customs Inventory Report.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the airline (or
other party who is acting for the airline).
To:
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of Customs
and/or Other Interested Parties, e.g. broker, Community System.

5. MESSAGE USE
The CSI message is sent at the completion of an update/amendment input to a
record in the airline in-house system.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Amend the origin of a simple air waybill shipment.

9. CUSTOMS SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION MESSAGE LAYOUT

CUSTOMS STATUS NOTIFICATION (CSN) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = CSN
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To update the inhouse system of the airline (or cargo terminal operator) with details
of Customs determination.
2.2 Where appropriate, to update the system of the airline (or cargo terminal operator)
with details of action taken by other Government agencies.
2.3 To notify the airline (or cargo terminal operator) of shipments required for
examination or released for delivery.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of Customs
and/or other Government agencies.
To:
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the airline (or
other party who is acting for the airline) and/or other Interested
Parties, e.g. broker, Community System.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 When the Customs system initiates (or is updated with details of) action effecting
the Customs status of a particular shipment a CSN message will be sent to the airline
(or the cargo terminal operator).
5.2 When a Government Agency places or releases a “hold” on a particular shipment
that Agency (in cooperation with Customs) will make the necessary input to trigger a
“hold” or “release hold” message to the airline (or the cargo terminal operator).

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 A Customs entry for a simple air waybill has been selected for goods and document
examination.

9. CUSTOMS STATUS NOTIFICATION MESSAGE LAYOUT

CASS DEBIT OR CREDIT MEMORANDUM (DCM) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = DCM
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To advise the CASS Settlement Office of an adjustment (debit or credit) to an air
waybill transaction which has already been invoiced by the Settlement Office.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of a CASS-EDI airline.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox.

5. MESSAGE USE
The DCM message is sent by an airline to the CASS Settlement Office to adjust air
waybill amounts previously invoiced to an agent. The Settlement Office will reflect
the adjustment in the subsequent invoice produced for the submitting airline.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Advice of corrections to an AWB transaction previously invoiced.

9. DEBIT OR CREDIT MEMORANDUM MESSAGE LAYOUT

AIRLINE CONFIRMATION (FAC) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FAC
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To confirm or further adjust any information previously transmitted in an Adjustment
Request (FAR) message.
2.2 To further adjust any information previously transmitted in a Freight Transaction
(FFT) or Air Waybill Data (FWB) message containing net billing information.
2.3 To confirm or further adjust any information previously transmitted in an Adjustment
Request (FAR) message after a CASS invoice has been issued.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of a CASS-EDI airline.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox; the
computer access address of a CASS-EDI agent.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 The Airline Confirmation message is to used by the CASS-EDI airline:
1. to confirm that any amount requested for adjustment is acceptable;
2. to further adjust any of the amounts transmitted in an Adjustment Request (FAR)
message;
3. to adjust any amount previously transmitted in a Freight Transaction (FFT) or Air
Waybill Data (FWB) message containing net billing information.
For AWB Reporting, the message is only valid if a Freight Transaction (FFT)
message or Air Waybill Data (FWB) message containing net billing information has
previously been transmitted to the CASS-EDI mailbox.
In this instance, the number of Airline Confirmation messages per air waybill
number is limited to 2.

9. AIRLINE CONFIRMATION MESSAGE LAYOUT

1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FAD

documentation found at destination, en route or at departure (see Cargo Services
Conference Resolutions Manual, Resolution 610 and Recommended Practice
1600q).

the station(s) as indicated in the Recommended Practice 1600q.

9. ADVICE OF DISCREPANCY MESSAGE LAYOUT

FREIGHT AGENT INFORMATION (FAI) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FAI
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To declare handling information for:
• each simple air waybill (covering a single shipment);
• each master air waybill (covering a group of consolidated “house” shipments);
• each individual “house” waybill (where the airline is breaking down a
consolidation and will control and deliver at the house waybill level);
• a special cargo shipment.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To
(Computer):

the Airline.
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
Nominated Broker and/or responsible Handling Agent or
party.
To (Manual): the predestined address of the Nominated Broker and/or
responsible Handling Agent or party.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 To inform the broker and handling parties of expected flight details before flight
arrival.
5.2 To inform the handling parties on nominated broker.
5.3 To provide the broker and handling parties with information such as cargo location,
arrival detail, total collect charges, storage location and customs origin code.
5.4 To provide basic air waybill information for broker and handling parties in case they
cannot receive an FWB/FSB Message.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES

simple air waybill shipment with the assumption that an FWB/FSB has already been
transmitted.

9. FREIGHT AGENT INFORMATION MESSAGE LAYOUT

ADJUSTMENT REQUEST (FAR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FAR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To request an adjustment to one of the monetary amount fields previously
transmitted in a Freight Transaction (FFT) or an FWB message containing net billing
information.
2.2 To request adjustments to CASS settlement amounts from a prior CASS billing
period for which a CASS invoice has been issued.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of a CASS-EDI agent.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox; the
computer access address of a CASS-EDI airline.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 This message is used by the CASS-EDI airline to consider a correction (adjustment)
to information previously transmitted to the CASS-EDI mailbox in a FFT or FWB
message containing net billing information.
Only one FAR message is allowed for each air waybill reported.
5.2 The message may also be to request adjustments once a CASS invoice has been
issued for a specified billing period.
Only one FAR message is allowed for each air waybill reported.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Request to adjust the currency exchange rate.

9. ADJUSTMENT REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

FREIGHT AGENT SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION (FAS) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FAS
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To update or amend handling information for:
• each simple air waybill (covering a single shipment);
• each master air waybill (covering a group of consolidated “house” shipments);
• each individual “house” waybill (where the airline is breaking down a
consolidation and will control and deliver at the house waybill level);
• supplied to a broker or handling parties in a FAI and/or previous FAS Messages;
• special cargo shipment.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To
(Computer):

the Airline.
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
Nominated Broker and/or responsible Handling Agent or
party.
To (Manual): the predestined address of the Nominated Broker and/or
responsible Handling Agent, or party.

5. MESSAGE USE
To advise changes, additions and deletions to the previous FAI or FAS Messages
after update/ amendment input to a record in the airline inhouse system.

9. FREIGHT AGENT SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION MESSAGE
LAYOUT

FREIGHT BOOKED LIST (FBL) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FBL
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To supply a complete list of consignments for which space has been reserved in a
particular flight, including details of the agent/airline from which the consignments
will be received and, if known, inward flight details as well.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To
(Computer):
To (Manual):

the handled carrier.
the access address for the Cargo Control Computer of the
handling party (carrier or agent).
the destination station office of the airline operating the
flight.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Intention
When a carrier is controlling his own flight but the physical handling of
consignments is carried out by a handling party (agent/airline), the former will issue
an FBL message to the latter to provide him with a complete list of consignments
for which space has been booked and any other relevant information.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Single destination list.
Ref. Message Content
1

FBL/4

2

1/KL791/19MAR/ZRH

3

LIS

4

074-71421280ZRHLIS/T20K54MC0.08/WATCHES

4

FBL1

Ref. 1
Ref.
9.3.3

For a SINGLE DESTINATION flight the Freight Booked
List comprises:
PART MESSAGE IDENTIFIER
1—
PART ORIGIN HEADER
2 — Occurs once only per message.
Comprises elements 2.1 thru 2.7.
PART DESTINATION HEADER
3 — Occurs once only per message.
Comprises elements 3.1 thru 3.3.
PART BOOKED CARGO
4 — Repeated for each booked consignment.
Comprises complete sets of consignment
information (elements 4.1 thru 9.3) for each
booked consignment.
PART LIST TRAILER
5 — Occurs once only per message.
Comprises an end code identifying the:
• end of a message (notification that a further
message relating to the same flight manifest
will follow, see note FBL4);
• end of list (notification that a list transmission
is complete).

If no consignment is booked for a particular destination airport the
DESTINATION HEADER for that airport is extended to include
element 3.2 (NIL Cargo Indication). The BOOKED CARGO
details which would normally follow a DESTINATION HEADER
are omitted.

Ref. 11 A Freight Booked List can be transmitted as a sequence of FBL
messages. (This is sometimes necessary due to message length
constraints imposed by the transmission network.)
Each individual message must commence with MESSAGE
IDENTIFIER, MANIFEST HEADER and DESTINATION
HEADER. Within the ORIGIN HEADER, a message sequence
number identifies the sequence in which individual FBL
messages have been transmitted.
The use of the code “CONT” (continued) in the LIST TRAILER at
the end of a FBL message signifies that a further message
relating to the same flight manifest will be transmitted.
The use of the code “LAST” in the LIST TRAILER at the end of a
FBL message signifies that the list transmission is complete.

FREIGHT BOOKED LIST REQUEST (FBR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FBR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To request a Freight Booked List (FBL) message.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To
(Computer):
To (Manual):

the handling party (carrier or agent).
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
handled carrier.
the destination station office of the handled carrier.

By handling parties (carriers or agents) to request a Freight Booked List (FBL)
message when needed.

9. FREIGHT BOOKED LIST REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

COURIER BAGGAGE VOUCHER (FBV) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FBV
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To exchange courier baggage voucher details in accordance with Recommended
Practice 1600g.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of a participant
involved in the movement of courier baggage.
To:
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of a participant
involved in the movement of courier baggage.

5. MESSAGE USE
To eliminate the need to re-enter Courier Baggage Voucher data which has already
been entered by a participant in the movement of courier baggage.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Exchange for courier bags going from Los Angeles to Tokyo.
Ref. Message Content
1

FBV/1

2

CBV/131-ABCD12345

3

9. COURIER BAGGAGE VOUCHER MESSAGE LAYOUT

CHARGES CORRECTION ACKNOWLEDGEMENT (FCA) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FCA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To notify the carrier issuing a Charges Correction Request (FCC) Message that the
request has been received and actioned.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party receiving the Charges Correction Request (FCC)
Message.
To:
the party (as indicated in the signature of the FCC Message) from
which the Charges Correction Request (FCC) Message was
received.

5. MESSAGE USE
—

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Acknowledge with minimum information.
Ref. Message Content
1

FCA

2

057-12345675

3

CID/057-C12345

5

ATH/23MAY85/CROYDON/LEWIS

6.2 Acknowledge with Other Special Information (OSI).
Ref. Message Content
1

FCA

2

026-24110004NBOMKC/24MAR82/NAIROBI

3

CID/015-C23456/KES/27MAR82/KANSAS CITY

4

9. CHARGES CORRECTION REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

CASS INVOICE (FCI) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FCI
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To advise the CASS-EDI agent of each air waybill transaction and the amount
payable in a given CASS billing period.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of the CASS Settlement Office.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox;
or
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI agent or airline
mailbox;
or
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI airline or the CASSEDI agent.

5. MESSAGE USE
The CASS EDI Invoice results from the processing of either the Freight Transaction
(FFT) or the net Air Waybill Data (FWB) message, with the Adjustment Request
(FAR) and the Airline Confirmation (FAC) messages transmitted by CASS-EDI
airlines and the CASS-EDI agents to the CASS-EDI mailbox.
The CASS Invoice message is transmitted to the CASS-EDI mailbox and/or directly
to the CASS-EDI airlines and agents.

9. CASS INVOICE MESSAGE LAYOUT

CASS REMITTANCE (FCR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FCR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To advise the CASS-EDI airline and the CASS-EDI agent of the total amounts due
by each party.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of the CASS Settlement Office.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox;
the computer access address of a CASS-EDI airline;
the computer access address of a CASS-EDI agent.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 The CASS Remittance message summarises the total amounts due by each
participant in the CASS-EDI settlement process after the CASS invoice procedure has
been completed.
The message is also transmitted to the CASS mailbox to advise the CASS-EDI
agents and airlines of the totals amounts due.
5.2 The CASS Remittance message may also be used for local CASS message
requirements and to transmit information to the CASS Settlement Bank.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES

9. CASS REMITTANCE MESSAGE LAYOUT

Data Element No. 519

CASS VOID/CANCEL AIR WAYBILL (FCV) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FCV
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To cancel or void an air waybill number and any transactions applied to that air
waybill in the CASS EDI procedures.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of the CASS-EDI airline.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox; the
computer access address of the CASS-EDI agent.

5. MESSAGE USE
A CASS-EDI airline may need to void or cancel an air waybill and to cancel any
CASS transactions that may have been applied against that air waybill.
Once this message is transmitted to the CASS mailbox, any transactions in the
mailbox are also voided.
The CASS Settlement Office will process voided air waybills as part of the
settlement process.
Cancelled air waybills will not be processed.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Voiding of one air waybill and cancellation of another.
Ref. Message Content
1 FCV/1

9. CASS VOID/CANCEL AIR WAYBILL MESSAGE LAYOUT

DISCREPANCY ANSWER (FDA) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FDA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To reply to an Advice of Discrepancy (FAD) Message to advise of action that will be
taken or should be taken.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party to which the Advice of Discrepancy (FAD) Message was
addressed.
To:
either:
the Advising Office Message Address optionally indicated as Ref.
5.3 in the Advice of Discrepancy (FAD) Message;
or:
if not included in the FAD Message — the party (as indicated in the
signature of the FAD message) from which the Advice of
Discrepancy (FAD) Message was received.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Situations Where an FDA Message is Not Required

8. MESSAGE NOTES
FDD1

Ref. 1

The numbers shown in column DGD Box No. corresponds with
the circled box numbers of the DGD form included as
ATTACHMENT 1.

FDD2

Ref.
1.1

Due to Cargo-IMP character set restrictions, the comma cannot
be transmitted. Therefore, two full stops will be used to indicate a
comma within the proper shipping name, technical name or
radioactive name.

FDD3

Ref.
2.3
Ref. 21 A Declaration for Dangerous Goods Data can be transmitted as a
sequence of FDD messages. (This is sometimes necessary due
to message length constraints imposed by the transmission
network).
Each individual FDD message must commence with MESSAGE
IDENTIFIER and DGD HEADER. Within the DGD HEADER a
message sequence number identifies the sequence in which
individual messages have been transmitted.
The use of the code “CONT” (continued) in the DGD TRAILER at
the end of a FDD message signifies that a further message

relating to the same Declaration for Dangerous Goods will be
transmitted.
The use of the code “LAST” in the DGD TRAILER at the end of a
FDD message signifies that the Declaration for Dangerous Goods
transmission is complete.

ATTACHMENT 1
EXAMPLE 4

AWB SPACE ALLOCATION ANSWER (FFA) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FFA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To reply to an AWB Space Allocation Request (FFR) Message indicating that
requested space can or cannot be confirmed.
2.2 To reply to an AWB Space Allocation Request (FFR) Message indicating that
request is being processed and that further FFA message will follow.
2.3 To reply to an AWB Space Allocation Request (FFR) Message confirming or
refusing the accepted updates by showing the new space allocation details.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Manual-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Multi-Airline Multi-Flight FFA Message
An airline will reply to a multi-airline multi-flight AWB Space Allocation Request
(FFR) Message using an FFA message which relates only to those space
allocations on flight(s) controlled by that airline.

5.2 Situations Where FFA Messages May Not Be Required
When cancellations (space allocation code “XX”), sale reports (space allocation
codes “CA” and “SS”) or background information (space allocation codes “HK” and
“HL”) are included in an AWB Space Allocation Request (FFR) Message and
accepted as such, an FFA Message may be sent at the discretion of the message
recipient.

9. AWB SPACE ALLOCATION ANSWER MESSAGE LAYOUT

AIRLINE FLIGHT MANIFEST (FFM) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FFM
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To notify details of consignments loaded onto a specified flight.
2.2 (optional)To notify details of the onward movements of consignment loaded onto a
specified flight to enable transfers to be preplanned.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To
(Computer):

the party generating the manifest.
the access address for the cargo control computer of the
airline, shed operator or handling agent receiving the
consignment.
To (Manual): the destination station office of the airline receiving the
consignment.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Multi-Airport FFM
A separate FFM is normally generated for each airport of unloading and only the
appropriate message is sent to each unloading point.
However, when generating an FFM to be sent to a central cargo system (which can
control the distribution of the load information to each unloading point) a single FFM
for multi-airports of unloading may be. sent. Cargo Control systems must therefore
be able to receive all of the following options:
• a series of single destination FFM messages (see note FFM1);
• a single multi destination FFM message (see note FFM2);
• a sequence of part FFM messages (see note FFM4).

manifest will follow, see note FFM4);
• end of manifest (notification that a
manifest transmission is complete).

FFM3

FFM4

Ref.
2.1

If no consignment is loaded for a particular destination airport the
DESTINATION HEADER for that airport is extended to include
element 3.2 (NIL Cargo Indication). The BULK LOADED and ULD
LOADED details which would normally follow a DESTINATION
HEADER are omitted.

Ref. 18 An airline Flight Manifest can be transmitted as a sequence of
FFM messages. (This is sometimes necessary due to message
length constraints imposed by the transmission network).
Each individual FFM message must commence with MESSAGE
IDENTIFIER, MANIFEST HEADER and DESTINATION
HEADER. In addition a ULD Detail Line must be included before
any sets of consignment information relating to ULD Loaded
Cargo (even if this ULD information has also been included in
previous FFM messages relating to the same flight). Within the
MANIFEST HEADER message sequence number identifies the
sequence in which individual messages have been transmitted.
The complete Consignment Detail/Consignment Onward
Movement Information (elements 4.1 thru 9.10) relating to one
consignment must always be sent in one FFM message.
The use of the code “CONT” (continued) in the MANIFEST
TRAILER at the end of a FFM message signifies that a further
message relating to the same flight manifest will be transmitted.
The use of the code “LAST” in the MANIFEST TRAILER at the
end of a FFM message signifies that the manifest transmission is
complete.

9. AIRLINE FLIGHT MANIFEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

AWB SPACE ALLOCATION REQUEST (FFR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FFR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To request that space on one or more flights be allocated for a nominated
consignment.
2.2 To request that the space allocated for a nominated consignment on one or more
flights be cancelled.
2.3 To request that the space allocated for a nominated consignment on one or more
flights be cancelled and replaced by a similar space allocation on another flight(s).
2.4 To add new information or to change/delete information to existing booking(s).

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Manual-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:

the party requesting space on flight(s) or updating existing
booking information.
To
the access address for the cargo control computer of the
(Computer): airline controlling the requested flight(s) or existing booking
(s).
To (Manual): the departure station office of the airline operating the
requested flight(s) or existing booking(s).

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Multi-Airline Multi-Flight FFR Message
A space allocation or an update to an existing booking may be requested for a
movement requiring carriage by several airlines on several flights by:
5.1.1 sending a separate “single airline” FFR message, i.e. a message listing the flight,
or flights, operated by one airline on which space is requested or an existing booking
updated, to each airline involved; OR
5.1.2 copying the same “multi-airline” FFR message, i.e. a message listing all the flights
on which space is requested or an existing booking updated, to each airline involved.

8. MESSAGE NOTES
FFR1

Ref.
1.1

Updating Principles
(a) Amendments permitted are shown in FFR
(b) The content of Ref. 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 shall
override the existing booking information.
(c) The only changes permitted to Ref. 3 — Flight Details are to
Ref. 3.5 — Space Allocation Code and Ref. 3.6.2 — Allotment
Identification.
(d) In case of deletion of all ULD, SSR, OSI, DIM, PID, SHP,
CNE, CUS and SRI information the ULD, SSR, OSI, DIM,
PID, SHP, CNE, CUS and SRI lines will be limited to the line
identifier only.

9. AWB SPACE ALLOCATION REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

FREIGHT TRANSACTION (FFT) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FFT
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To advise the CASS Settlement Office of specific Air Waybill transaction data
received by the CASS-EDI airline from a CASS-EDI cargo agent.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the computer access address of a CASS-EDI airline.
To:
the computer access address of the CASS-EDI mailbox;
the computer access address of a CASS-EDI agent.

5. MESSAGE USE
The Freight Transaction message is transmitted by a CASS-EDI airline to the
CASS-EDI mailbox to begin the CASS-EDI settlement process when the FWB
message does not include net billing information.
The CASS-EDI mailbox may further transmit the message to the appropriate
CASS-EDI agent.
The Freight Transaction message may be used in conjunction with the Adjustment
Request (FAR) and the Airline Confirmation (FAC) messages to agree “net
amounts” or to adjust other amounts, i.e. the adjustment process, prior to the CASS
invoicing procedure.
Alternatively, the message may be transmitted by the CASS-EDI airline to the
CASS-EDI mailbox after the adjustment process has been completed by the CASSEDI airline and CASS-EDI agent.
The message may be used on a transaction-by-transaction basis or on a list basis.

9. PIECE STATUS ANSWER MESSAGE LAYOUT

PIECE MANIFEST (FPM) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FPM
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To provide individual piece identification numbers to a carrier.
2.2 To reply to a Piece Manifest Request (FPR) message.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Manual-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party requiring piece level tracking.
To:
the party providing piece level tracking.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Shippers or Forwarders who expect tracking of their consignments at the piece level
will send this message to the airline responsible for the shipment.
5.2 Airlines that provide tracking of their customers’ consignments at the piece level will
forward this message to other airlines when interlining occurs.

1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FRR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To request the description corresponding to:
• a specific Rate Note;
• a specific Commodity Item Number;
• a specific ULD Charge Code.

Computer-to-Computer.

agent requesting a description.

9. SUPPLEMENTARY RATE INFORMATION REQUEST MESSAGE
LAYOUT

STATUS ANSWER (FSA) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FSA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To reply to a Status Request (FSR) Message indicating latest status, or statuses, in
the movement of the nominated consignment.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From
(Manual):

the airline, shed operator or handling agent to which the
Status Request (FSR) Message was addressed.

From
(Computer):

the access address of the cargo control computer of the
airline, shed operator, or handling agent actioning the
consignment movement.
To
the access address of the cargo control computer (as
(Computer): indicated in the signature of the FSR Message) from which
the Status Request (FSR) Message was sent.
To (Manual): the party (as indicated in the signature of the FSR message)
from which the Status Request (FSR) Message was
received.

9. STATUS ANSWER MESSAGE LAYOUT

SUBSTITUTE AIR WAYBILL DATA (FSB) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FSB
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To transmit available Air Waybill data in response to a FWR message.
2.2 To transmit available Air Waybill data from one participant involved in the movement
of a consignment to another participant.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer/Manual-toManual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From
(Manual):
From
(Computer):

the originating (or any other) participant involved in the
movement of a consignment.
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
originating (or any other) participant involved in the
movement of a consignment.
To (Manual): the Message Address of the requestor as indicated in the
last line of the FWR message.
To
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
(Computer): FWR requestor or any other participant.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Computer Environment
To provide all available Air Waybill data when complete Air Waybill data is not
available.

5.2 Manual Environment
To provide Air Waybill data according to the Cargo Services Conference
Resolutions Manual, Recommended Practice 1600s.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES

9. STATUS REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

STATUS UPDATE (FSU) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FSU
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To notify/update interested parties with a (change of) status of a specified
consignment as recorded in the system of a handling party.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
the handling party (airline, handling agent ...).
To
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of the
(Computer): Interested Party.
To
the pre-destined address of the Interested Party.
(Manual):

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 When to send an FSU — an FSU is sent, by bilateral agreement, for a shipment or
each part of shipment after a specified status has been recorded in the Handling Party’s
system for that particular shipment or part shipment.
5.2 The format of the FSU Message is the same as the FSA Message except that the
FSU Message can only be used as follows:
— for one non-repeatable status or the Other Customs, Security Control and
Regulatory Control Information (OCI) line and may be accompanied by the optional
ULD description
— for one non-repeatable status and accompanied by the optional Other Customs,
Security Control and Regulatory Control Information (OCI) line and/or ULD
description.
The Note FSA52 does not apply.

9. RATE INFORMATION REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

ULD SPACE ALLOCATION ANSWER (FUA) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FUA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To reply to a ULD Space Allocation Request (FUR) Message indicating that
requested space can or cannot be confirmed.
2.2 To reply to a ULD Space Allocation Request (FUR) Message indicating that request
is being processed and that a further FUA message will follow.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the airline controlling the requested flight(s).
To:
the party (as indicated in the last line of the FUR message) who
requested space on the flight(s).

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Multi-Airline Multi-Flight FUA Message
An airline will reply to a multi-airline multi-flight ULD Space Allocation Request
(FUR) Message using a FUA message which relates only to those space
allocations on flight(s) controlled by that airline.

5.2 Situation Where FUA Messages Are Not Required
When cancellation (allocation action code “XX”), sale reports (allocation action
codes “CA” and “SS”) and background information (allocation action codes “HK”
and “HL”) are included in a ULD Space Allocation Request (FUR) Message, there is
no need for an acknowledgement by a FUA message.

9. ULD SPACE ALLOCATION ANSWER MESSAGE LAYOUT

UNIT LOAD DEVICE MANIFEST (FUM) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FUM
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 The Electronic representation of a ULD Tag at ULD build up (Export), i.e.:
• to notify details of consignments (air waybills and/or house air waybills) loaded into a
specific Unit Load Device (= ULD); or
• to notify details of cargo loaded or empty ULD loaded on or into another ULD (e.g.
sub ULDs in main ULDs, piggybacked ULDs or pallet stacks).
2.2 (optional) To notify details of consignments loaded into a specific ULD to enable
transfers to be preplanned.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:

the party generating the manifest (ULD Tag) or accepting a
Shipper built unit (BUP), in general a General Handling
Agent.
To
the access address for the cargo control computer of the
(Computer): airline.
To: (Manual): the station office (office function designator = FF) of the
airline where the Unit Load Device was created/accepted.

5. MESSAGE USE
A FUM is generated wherever a Unit Load Device is being built up (be it with cargo
or without) in conjunction to the creation of a ULD Tag (or group of Tags in the case
sub ULDs were used). The time stamp of ULD Build up event (= preparation) is
kept in the ULD Manifest Header (see Part 2).
A FUM message allows airlines to get immediately notified of cargo and ULD build
up at export stations. One FUM message shall be generated per main ULD (a main
ULD might contain sub ULDs).
For the physical preparation of cargo to be loaded in the aircraft bulk hold a
fictitious ULD number may be used, e.g. BLK00000CV, for internal use only. In
practice, the combination of all generated FUM messages for one flight could
correspond to the later sent FFM and UCM messages for this flight).
Correction of the FUM message shall be handled in overwrite mode, i.e. the last
message will always count.

FUM3 Ref. 6. A ULD Description line (Ref. 3.) followed by a ULD Inclusion
Information (Ref. 6.) indicates that the ULD stated in the ULD
Description line is a sub ULD to the ULD stated in the ULD
Inclusion Information line (the last mentioned being the main
ULD).
FUM4 Ref. 7. A ULD Description line (Ref. 3.) followed by a ULD Connection
Information (Ref. 7.) indicates that the ULD stated in the ULD
Description line is connected to another ULD, i.e. the one being
stated in the ULD Connection Information line.

8.1
A ULD Manifest can be transmitted as a sequence of FUM messages. (This is
sometimes necessary due to message length constraints imposed by the
transmission network).

Each individual FUM message must commence with MESSAGE IDENTIFIER, ULD
MANIFEST HEADER, ULD DESTINATION HEADER.
In addition, either an Empty Equipment in Compartment line (Ref. 8.) or a
Consignment Detail line (Ref. 9.) must be included in the message.
The Consignment detail line might (should) also include any optional Dimensions,
Consignment Onward Movement, Movement Priority Information, Handling
Information, Other Service Information and Special Customs Information lines (if
available), which must be included before any sets of House waybill information
even if this Consignment related information has also been included in previous
FUM messages.
Each individual FUM Message will always end with a MANIFEST COMPLETE
INDICATOR.

9. UNIT LOAD DEVICE MANIFEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

ULD SPACE ALLOCATION REQUEST (FUR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FUR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To request that ULD space on one or more flights be allocated against a unique
request identifier.
2.2 To request that ULD space on one or more flights be cancelled.
2.3 To request that the ULD space allocated on one or more flights be cancelled and
replaced by a similar space allocation on another flight(s).

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Manual-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party requesting space on flight(s).
To:
the departure station office of the airline operating the requested
flight(s).

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Multi-Airline Multi-Flight FUR Message
A ULD space allocation may be requested for a movement requiring carriage by
several airlines on several flights by:
5.1.1 sending a separate “single airline” FUR message, i.e. a message listing the flight,
or flights, operated by one airline on which space is requested, to each airline involved;
OR
5.1.2 copying the same “multi airline” FUR message, i.e. a message listing all the flights
on which space is requested, to each airline involved.

5.2 ULD Space Allocation Request Identification
An FUR message is a space allocation request for multiple consignments
contained in one or more ULDs. As the request cannot be linked to a single air
waybill reference, a single “Booking File Reference” is used (see Message Ref.
2.1).

5.3 Situation Where an FUR Message is Not Required
Where a space allocation is required for a single consignment contained in one or
more ULDs, an AWB Space Allocation Request (FFR) Message must be used.

8. MESSAGE NOTES
FUR1

Ref.
2.1

The initial ULD Space Allocation Request (FUR) Message does
not include a “Booking File Reference”. This reference is issued
by the airline when allocating the requested ULD space. FUR
Messages requesting flight amendments and all FUA answer
messages must include this “Booking File Reference”.

FUR20 Ref.
2.2

ULD Quantity (for which space has been requested).

FUR21 Ref.
3.5

Space Allocation Code (see Code List, 1.7(a) and 1.7(c)).

FUR22 Ref.
4.5.3

ULD Owner Code (if 4.5.2 included).

FUR23 Ref.
7.3

Requesting Office Message Address (to which FUA is to be sent).

FUR24 Ref.
3.6

Allotment Identification (if Space Allocation Code (Ref. 3.5)
is“CA”).

9. ULD SPACE ALLOCATION REQUEST MESSAGE LAYOUT

SCHEDULE AND AVAILABILITY INFORMATION ANSWER (FVA)
MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FVA
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To reply to a Schedule and Availability Information Request (FVR) Message
indicating the schedule and availability information selected. Availability information
will be provided at the option of the party, i.e. carrier, being requested for this
information.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the access address of the cargo control computer of the party to
which the Schedule and Availability Information Request (FVR)
Message was addressed.
To:
the access address of the cargo control computer of the cargo
agent from which the Schedule and Availability Information Request
(FVR) Message was sent.

9. SCHEDULE AND AVAILABILITY INFORMATION ANSWER
MESSAGE LAYOUT

SCHEDULE AND AVAILABILITY INFORMATION REQUEST (FVR)
MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FVR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To request Schedule Information (on direct flights and connections of up to three
flights) for a specific routing on either a specific date or for a period of a month; and
Availability Information for a specific routing on a specific date for either a specific
flight or for all direct flights and connections of up to three flights.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the access address of the cargo control computer of the cargo
agent requesting the Schedule and Availability Information.
To:
the access address of the cargo control computer of the party
responsible for the display of the Schedule and Availability
Information.

FVR20 Ref.
2.5

Date
When a Day of Month is not specified, schedule is being
requested for a specific month.
When a Day of Month is specified, schedule and availability is
being requested for a specific date.

FVR21 Ref.

Separator (if one of 2.7, 2.9, 2.11, 2.13 or 2.15 included).

2.6
FVR22 Ref.
2.7

Carrier/Flight
When a Flight Number is not specified, schedule and availability
is being requested for a routing:
• comprising the flights of all airlines when a Carrier Code is not
specified;
• comprising only the flights (or first flights in case of
combinations) of a specified airline when a Carrier Code is
specified.
When a Flight Number is specified, schedule and availability is
being requested for this flight only.

FVR23 Ref.
2.8

Separator (if one of 2.9, 2.11, 2.13 or 2.15 included).

FVR24 Ref.
2.9

Earliest Departure Time
When an Earliest Departure Time is not specified, schedule and
availability is being requested for all flights (or first flights in case
of combinations) departing from 00h00.
When an Earliest Departure Time is specified, schedule and
availability is being requested for flights (or first flights in case of
combinations) departing from the specified time.

FVR25 Ref.
2.10

Separator (if one of 2.11, 2.13 or 2.15 included).

FVR26 Ref.
2.11

Latest Arrival Date/Time
When a Latest Arrival Date/Time is not specified, schedule and
availability is being requested for all flights.
When the Latest Arrival Date is specified and the Latest Arrival
Time is not specified, schedule and availability is being requested
for those flights (or last flights in case of combinations) that arrive
at the destination no later than 23h59 on the specified date.
When both the Latest Arrival Date and Time are specified,
schedule and availability is being request for those flights (or last
flights in case of combinations) that arrive at the destination no
later than the specified date/time.

9. SCHEDULE AND AVAILABILITY INFORMATION REQUEST
MESSAGE LAYOUT

AIR WAYBILL DATA (FWB) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FWB
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To transmit a complete set of Air Waybill data in accordance with the Cargo
Services Conference Resolutions Manual.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:

the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of a
participant involved in the movement of a consignment.
To
the access address of the Cargo Control Computer of a
(Computer): participant involved in the movement of a consignment.
To (Manual): the message address of the requestor for Air Waybill data
as indicated in the last line of the FWR message.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Intention
To eliminate the need to re-enter Air Waybill data which has been already entered
by an earlier participant in the movement of a consignment.
To eliminate the need for the paper copy of an air waybill to accompany the
consignment in accordance with ICAO Annex 9, Section B, Chapter 4.
5.2 Various cases where a FWB message is used:
• when a cargo agent delivers a consignment to an airline;
• when an airline transfers a consignment to another airline;
• when an airline delivers a consignment to a handling party;
• when a handling party delivers a consignment to an airline;
• when an airline delivers a consignment to a cargo agent;
• when a participant requests Air Waybill data by a FWR message.
5.3 When to send an automatic FWB message:
• an unsolicited FWB message must be sent prior to the physical delivery of the goods.

5. MESSAGE USE
5.1 Various Cases Where a FWR Message is Used
5.1.1 Computer Environment:
• when a system is unable to receive unsolicited FWB message;
• when system-to-system connections are not permanent;
• when recipient of a FWB message cannot be determined by origin system;
• when an automatically generated FWB message failed to be received.
5.1.2 Manual Environment:
• when Air Waybill data is required to issue a “Substitute Air Waybill”.

9. HOUSE WAYBILL STATUS ANSWER MESSAGE LAYOUT

HOUSE WAYBILL STATUS UPDATE (FZE) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = FZE
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To notify a new status of a specified house waybill consignment.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: The party facing the change of status.
To:
The access address of the cargo control computer of the party
needing to be advised of the change of status.

5. MESSAGE USE
The format of the FZE Message is the same as the FZD Message except that the
FZE Message can only be used for one non-repeatable status.

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Consignment delivered to consignee or his agent.
Ref. Message Content
1

FZE/5

2

HCD/077-12345675/123456789/BOGNCE/T10K350

15 DLV/03NOV1615/NCE/T10K350/MICLARK
Notes
1. Refer to FZD Message Examples for other FZE Message Examples (FZD 6.1 to
6.14, 6.16 and 6.18 only).
2. Refer to FZD Message Specifications, Notes and Layout for FZE Message
Specifications, Notes and Layout.
Following Exceptions apply:
— Note under 2.7 should read:
Ref. 2 must be followed by one of the optional Ref. 3 to 20 possibly with the
optional Ref. 22.
— Last Note(s) of each Ref. 3 to 20 do not apply.
3. The FZE Message Type Version Number is the same as the FZD Message Type
Version Number.

9. MAIL ADVISORY MESSAGE LAYOUT

MAIL LABEL DATA (MLD) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = MLD
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To provide bar coded label data for mail receptacles and related information for
mail to an airline contracting ground handling services for the mail.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party providing ground handling services for mail.
To:
the airline contracting the ground handling services for mail.

5. MESSAGE USE
The message is designed and intended to be used within an airport environment by
parties providing ground handling services to an airline for mail receptacles. These
parties are not anticipated to have interfaces with the designated postal operators
but do have interfaces with the airlines.
The individual mail label data, journey identifiers and identification of units used for
the mail receptacles, e.g. ULD, belly cart, general container, can be included in the
message along with the particular status event indication as well as other relevant
information, e.g. flights, date/times, locations, airline and designated postal
operator identification, etc. This advises the airline contracting the ground services
for the mail as to what has occurred with the receptacles.
The airline may then use this information to compose and provide a status update
to the appropriate designated postal operator using the conventional Universal
Postal Union (UPU) standard EDIFACT Message (RESDIT).

9. SURFACE TRANSPORTATION BOOKING ANSWER MESSAGE
LAYOUT

SURFACE TRANSPORTATION BOOKING REQUEST (SBR) MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = SBR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
To request booking by motor carrier of:
• shipper-to-airport consignment for pickup;
• airport-to-consignee consignment for delivery;
• airport-to-airport pickup and delivery of manifested consignments.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From:
To (Computer):

Airline or Air Forwarder.
Motor Carrier.

5. MESSAGE USE
—

6. MESSAGE EXAMPLES
6.1 Request to a surface transport provider for pickup from the shipper of a House
Waybill consignment associated with a Master Air Waybill.
Ref. Message Content
1

SBR/4

2

DOC//125-12345675M/AEI1234567

3

ACD/LONPAR/T1K750/TEXTILES

4

FLT/BA1234//19SEP1200/LHRCDG/NN

5

SSR/SPECIAL CARE REQUIRED

6

OSI/CONTACT AGENT PRIOR TO PICKUP AT STAINES

7

8

Ref. 1. — Updating Principles

9. SURFACE TRANSPORTATION PLANNING ANSWER MESSAGE
LAYOUT

SURFACE TRANSPORTATION PLANNING REQUEST (SPR)
MESSAGE
1. STANDARD MESSAGE IDENTIFIER = SPR
2. MESSAGE FUNCTION
2.1 To request a terminal slot for a motor carrier to pickup or deliver consignments.
2.2 To advise of vehicle and consignment details.
2.3 To advise of changes to terminal slot related information.

3. MESSAGE APPLICATION
Computer-to-Computer/Computer-to-Manual/Manual-to-Computer.

4. MESSAGE EXCHANGE PARTIES
From: the party requesting the terminal slot.
To:
the party providing the terminal slot.

5. MESSAGE USE
—
